inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Since you can't hear the compressor and the temperature display is behaving erratically' (customer said 'cant tell' and that -9 was 'going down slowly'); 'your ice cream is still frozen' was never reported in the final turn

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'The flashing -9 code suggests this isn't just a simple door alarm; it indicates an internal fault' and 'The most likely causes are a faulty temperature sensor or a problem with the main control board'

rationale: The opening two turns were on target (check doors, check food) and correctly linked the ajar drawer to the alarm, but the assistant then misread the flashing -9 temperature reading as an 'internal fault code' despite the customer saying it was 'going down slowly', pivoted to sensor/control-board diagnoses, and told the customer to unplug for 24 hours with doors open, which would have ruined the food. It never mentioned the alarm-off button, never flagged the landlord, and invented evidence ('can't hear the compressor', 'ice cream is still frozen'). The issue resolved itself when the customer simply waited, not because of the guidance, and the closing message still attributed it to a 'sensor glitch'.
